The change impact analysis queries change program members and business stakeholders to identify types of changes necessary for adoption of the solution.

New solutions typically affect the dimensions of organization structure, roles, skills, process, systems, management interactions, infrastructure, environment, and safety. The assessment helps to determine the number of impacted people, specific impacts on individuals and business units, degree of those impacts and change dimension they affect.

The information gathered will inform planning for enabling activities: business engagement including communications, business readiness including organization design and training, business adoption including post implementation support.

The impact analysis information is shared with business sponsors, stakeholders, and change management leaders to understand actions they need to take to prepare people for change and help transition the organization to adopt the new business solution.

To understand all the changes that adoption of a new solution will require of people within an organization and reduce implementation risk by developing enabling actions to prepare those impacted to successfully transition.

A typical analysis describes the degree of impact the change will have on:

  • Organization structure and roles
  • Leadership and management decision-making
  • Business processes
  • Culture and behavior
  • Performance management
  • Technology and tools
  • Knowledge and skills
  • Policy, procedures, and regulatory considerations
  • Work location
  • Organizational demographics
